function:rack::system::openBrowser(const.finding: P1: the shell-character guard is applied on Windows too, where it is unjustified. requireShellSafe (native/bindings/services/system.cpp:50-54, 167-169) refuses \", \\, $ and ` on every platform. Only Linux (`xdg-open \"...\"`) and macOS (`open \"...\"`) go through std::system; Windows calls ShellExecuteW with no shell (Rack src/system.cpp:868-890). docs/reference/services.md:156-158 explains the guard by xdg-open only. Smallest fix: wrap the check in `#if !defined ARCH_WIN`, and document it per platform (xdg-open on Linux, open on macOS, none on Windows).

function:rack::system::openDirectory(con.finding: P1: open_directory refuses every native Windows path. requireShellSafe rejects '\\' (native/bindings/services/system.cpp:50-54, 171-175), and os.fspath of a Windows path contains backslashes, yet Rack's Windows openDirectory uses ShellExecuteW 'explore' with no shell (Rack src/system.cpp:892-914). The test is also weak: test_system.py:163 only calls open_directory(\"\"), a no-op that passes even if nothing is bound, and the refusal is tested only for open_browser. Smallest fix: skip the guard on ARCH_WIN, document it per platform, and add a refusal test for open_directory (ideally also a PATH-stubbed xdg-open on Linux that records its argument).

function:rack::system::setFpuFlags(uint3.finding: P1: invalid flags crash the host, and this is neither guarded nor documented. set_fpu_flags passes any uint32 straight to Rack (native/bindings/services/system.cpp:186), which calls _mm_setcsr on x64 (Rack src/system.cpp:947-953). Setting any reserved MXCSR bit (16-31) raises #GP, which is SIGSEGV on Linux, so `rsys.set_fpu_flags(1 << 16)` kills Rack. Unmasking FP exceptions (bits 7-12) makes the interpreter's own float arithmetic on that thread raise SIGFPE. docs/reference/services.md:149-154 mentions neither. Smallest fix: on x64, refuse flags with bits outside 0xFFFF (ValueError), document that unmasking exceptions crashes Python, and test the refusal.

function:rack::system::setThreadName(con.finding: P1: no assertion checks the effect. tests/services/in_rack_system/test_system.py:140-148 only checks that the call returns (`names == ['ok']`), so a no-op binding passes. Rack sets the name with pthread_setname_np on Linux, truncated to 15 bytes (Rack src/system.cpp:657-665). Smallest fix: on Linux, read /proc/self/task/<threading.get_native_id()>/comm in the worker and assert 'rackpy-worker'. Add a long name to check the truncation, and document that Rack does nothing on macOS and Windows.

function:rack::system::sleep(double).finding: P1: the negative-time refusal is unjustified and undocumented. native/bindings/services/system.cpp:160-165 raises ValueError for time < 0, and the test asserts that (test_system.py:135-136). But Rack's sleep is std::this_thread::sleep_for(duration<double>(time)) (Rack src/system.cpp:821-823), which returns at once for non-positive durations; only NaN/inf (and huge finite values, which the guard lets through) reach undefined conversion. docs/reference/services.md:145-146 lists `sleep(seconds)` with no restriction. Smallest fix: pass negative values through to Rack, refuse only non-finite or out-of-range values, and document the refusal in services.md#services-system.
